selected_image.visual_review: Direct original review shows open red-column pavilions above water, connected by a covered gallery with green posts, low geometric rails and gray stone/concrete platforms supported above the water. Gray tiled eaves have round tile ends; blue/green/gold beam paintings and red hanging lanterns separate the timber members. Reflections show the underside clearance and platform supports. The gallery identifies this as Ouxiang; no building name is legible within the selected image itself. No exact dimensions, six-seat furniture layout, original seventeenth-century construction or night lighting are established.

collection_notes: All three gallery originals were directly inspected. First shows a closed waterside hall; second shows a willow/rock shoreline. The third matches the required open water-pavilion structure. Only the third fills the architecture slot; no night or extra foliage/material slot is counted.
